claim: Harry was pleased that he avoided buying Cherki or Foden for GW3 and instead retained Mbeumo, who scored.
quote: I decided not to buy either Turkey or Phil Fton into my team and keep hold of Bran and Burmo, a decision I'm pretty happy with.

claim: Harry confirmed that he sold Bruno Fernandes for Cole Palmer ahead of GW4.
quote: Bruno Fernandez went out of my team of course he blanked away at Everton and Cole Palmer came in at home to Hull.

claim: Harry confirmed that he sold Tzolis for Morgan Gibbs-White ahead of GW4.
quote: This freed up a bit of money which allow me to do solace up to Morgan Gibbs White

claim: Harry confirmed that his third GW4 transfer was Rodon to Muharemović.
quote: And then I also sold Rodon. Now, this was the position that I was least certain of

claim: Harry considers Chelsea's home match against Hull a fixture worth targeting despite Hull's three clean sheets because the underlying chance data remains poor.
quote: I still think it is a fixture that we want to take hold of as much as possible with the likes of Palmer, Rogers, and Jal Pedro.

claim: Harry likes Gibbs-White's next three fixtures: Aston Villa away, Coventry at home and Crystal Palace away.
quote: Aston Villa away, Coventry at home, Crystal Palace away in the next three games. I really like him.

claim: Harry described Gibbs-White as Nottingham Forest's set-piece and penalty taker as well as their main open-play threat.
quote: Nottingham Forest set peace taker, penalty taker, and just their main open play threat.

claim: Harry acted early on Rodon because he was predicted to fall in price, even though this prevented him waiting for Arsenal team information.
quote: Roodon was the one predicted to drop in price. So, I had to act early and couldn't wait to see who started for Arsenal

claim: Harry likes Muharemović for home matches against Newcastle and Crystal Palace before his planned GW6 wildcard, citing defensive-contribution and attacking potential.
quote: Newcastle at home and Crystal Palace at home before I still plan on playing my wild card in gameweek six at the very latest.

claim: Harry considered Pedro Porro and Van Hecke instead of Muharemović but disliked doubling Spurs defence alongside Kinsky.
quote: The other two that I really did consider was Pedro Porro or Van Heck of Spurs.

claim: With the benefit of the GW3 line-ups, Harry says his defender decision would have been between Muharemović, Ben White and Konsa.
quote: If I had the decision again, it probably would be Mahmraovic versus Ben White versus Ezri Konza.

claim: Harry saw Timber's possible return to the Arsenal squad as a potential threat to Ben White's place.
quote: I didn't know if Timber was going to be back in the Arsenal squad, which was going to become an issue for Ben White.

claim: Harry was uncertain which of Konsa and Mosquera would start for Arsenal when he made his transfer.
quote: I didn't know if Ezri Konza or Mosca was going to start, which was going to be an issue for buying Ezri Konza.

claim: Harry currently plans to start Verbruggen over Kinsky in GW4, although he rates their clean-sheet chances almost identically.
quote: They're actually ranked at almost exactly the same chance of keeping a clean sheet. Verugan goes away to Coventry and Kinsky has Everton at home.

claim: Harry views Kinsky at home to Everton as a close benching call but currently prefers Verbruggen because Everton's attack has looked respectable.
quote: At the moment I'm going with Verugan away at Coventry. I just think Everton have looked not bad.

claim: Harry is disappointed with Szoboszlai's attacking threat and defensive-contribution reliability while he spends minutes at right-back, though he will likely hold for Fulham.
quote: I'm not sure his attacking return looks good enough and he is still playing some minutes at right back and not hitting Defcon 100%

claim: Harry currently has Mbeumo benched for Gomez but regards it as unresolved because the fixture favours Gomez while player quality favours Mbeumo.
quote: the fixture would say I should play Gomez, but the player should say I would play Brian and Burmo

claim: Harry will revisit Mbeumo versus Gomez after European matches, noting that Gomez has no midweek fixture while Manchester United play on Thursday.
quote: Brri and Burmo whereas Gomez has a full midweek off because Brighton don't play in Europe this midweek

claim: Harry's GW4 captaincy is a close choice between João Pedro and Palmer, with one certain to receive his armband.
quote: At the moment, the plan will be to captain either Ja Pedro or Cole Palmer. It's pretty close between the two.

claim: Harry advises managers who can wait to delay transfers until after the midweek European matches because rotation and injuries are now relevant.
quote: discussions around rolling transfers until later on in the week if you're able to do it. potential rotation around European competitions

claim: Harry says all three Chelsea attackers offer good value and sees scope for a triple-up on a free hit or wildcard because Chelsea have no European congestion.
quote: I all think they offer really good value. So if you're on a free hit potentially you want a wild card

claim: Harry ranks João Pedro clearly ahead of Palmer and Rogers as the best Chelsea attacking pick due to price, position and expected season-long returns.
quote: Jedro is for me head and shoulders above both Palmer and Rogers. It's a nice forward spot. He's cheaper than Palmer

claim: For the short-term Hull fixture, Harry prefers Palmer over Rogers because Palmer has the greater explosive-return ceiling.
quote: you do probably want to prioritize the player that is more explosive and has the ability to get that higher upside huge return

claim: Harry expects Palmer to take Chelsea's penalties, reinforcing his short-term upside.
quote: And we expect him to be on penalties for Chelsea.

claim: Harry says Rogers rather than Palmer can make long-term squad structures containing Bruno Fernandes or Saka affordable.
quote: if you were to go for Rogers and it might allow you to own Bruno Fernandez or Bay Saka

claim: Harry's illustrative GW4 wildcard draft starts with a triple Arsenal defence of Raya, Calafiori and Konsa.
quote: it's a triple up on the ass defense with David Ry, Cal Fury, and Ezri Coner.

claim: Harry worries that Raya and Konsa offer limited upside and that triple Arsenal defence blocks higher-upside Arsenal attackers later.
quote: My concern is is it blocks someone like Martin Odigard, Solless of course who started again for Arsenal, but most likely Bkai Saka

claim: Harry sees Van Hecke as a possible wildcard alternative to Konsa because Spurs defended well and have a good long-term fixture run.
quote: I could go for Kza to someone like a Van Hec of Spurs who I do think defended pretty well

claim: Harry says De Cuyper is on set pieces and playing at left wing, though Brighton's fixtures are mixed.
quote: D Kyper is in onset pieces playing left wing. They have some mixed fixtures

claim: Harry says De Cuyper rotates well with Thiaw and Egan in his wildcard draft.
quote: he does rotate pretty well with Malik Chow and Egan.

claim: Harry likes Groß operating as Brighton's number 10 while Hinshelwood is injured.
quote: Pascal Gross, who looks great in the number 10 whilst Hinchwood is out injured

claim: Harry uses Mbeumo as cheaper Manchester United attacking coverage when omitting Bruno Fernandes from his wildcard draft.
quote: is to cover a little bit of that Manchester United attack who I still think will play well even with Europe.

claim: Harry does not plan to select Bruno Fernandes on wildcard and recommends against paying £12 million for him.
quote: my recommendation wouldn't be to spend 12 million on him

claim: Harry's illustrative GW4 wildcard forward line is Wissa, João Pedro and Haaland.
quote: And then up front, it's Yoan Vissa, J Pedro, and Erling Harland.

claim: Harry's illustrative free-hit draft targets Chelsea, Brighton, Arsenal and Liverpool, with one defender captioned ambiguously as Bayas.

claim: Harry currently plans not to wildcard or free hit in GW4 because his existing team looks good for both GW4 and GW5.
quote: the big reason that the moment I'm not planning on playing a chip despite the fact that I've used three transfers

claim: Harry plans to roll in GW5 and wildcard in GW6 over the international break, leaving two transfers banked for GW7.

claim: A significant midweek injury affecting Harry's starting XI would likely make him wildcard, while he considers a free hit much less likely.
quote: if there's a big injury that changes the way that my team is looking and I've got to make a transfer

claim: Harry says fear about insufficient Arsenal coverage or not owning Isak could make the GW4 free hit attractive.
quote: if I get scared about Arsenal, if I get scared about not having Alexander Isac, then absolutely the free hit does look really good.

claim: Harry expects Maguire may fall in price and thinks Mbeumo might fall again, although Mbeumo's latest goal could prevent it.
quote: Harry McGuire is probably going to drop. Brandon Burmo might drop again, although he's just scored, so I might be all right with that.
